issues.description: The solution repository introduces an interface named Dairy (Dairy.java) and has an empty Milkable.java, while the problem statement and template refer to an interface named Milkable with method messageOnMilk(). Several solution classes (Seal, Goat) implement Dairy instead of Milkable. This name/type mismatch between Milkable (specified) and Dairy (implemented) is structural and will confuse students and tests that expect a Milkable interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name and usage across artifacts. Rename Dairy.java to Milkable.java (or implement Milkable with messageOnMilk()) and remove the empty Milkable.java. Update Seal.java and Goat.java to implement Milkable (or update the problem statement/template to reference Dairy consistently). Ensure the interface defines String messageOnMilk() as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the milk-related interface as 'Milkable', but the solution implementation defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (and classes implement Dairy). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual interface (milkable behavior) can confuse students mapping the requirements to the provided/expected implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface (file and type) to 'Milkable' and update all classes that implement it (Seal, Goat, etc.) to implement Milkable; or alternatively change the problem statement and template references to 'Dairy'. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem statement by renaming Dairy -> Milkable to avoid student confusion.
